text.p: - The new Slovenian parliament started its first session on Thursday but has not yet elected a president. The session will continue next Monday.

- Centre-left Liberal Democrats of current Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek met heads of rightist "Spring" parties on Thursday evening but no agreement was reached with both sides insisting on their candidate for prime minister.
- Interior Minister Andrej Ster attended a meeting in Brussels on crime in Europe on Thursday.

- The manangement of troubled machines producer Litostroj has designed several rehabilitation programmes to bring the company back into the black. It is up to the owners now to decide which programme to undertake.
- Slovenians will take part in a referendum on December 8, to choose between three diferent electoral models.
- Exporters are searching for ways of lowering expenses in order to overcome 3.5 percent higher electricity prices that will come into force on December 5.
- Slovenian October industrial output was 3.1 percent higher than in September, the Statistical Office said.
- The Privatisation Agency may propose to the government that it should manage state companies in the future.
